subject: Reconciling multipath access for private inference: PrivateLink vs Peering vs S2S VPN
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@orionhealth.com>, Bob Nguyen <bob.nguyen@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reconciling multipath access for private inference: PrivateLink vs Peering vs S2S VPN

Hi Alice & Bob —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Per Orion's compliance and latency goals, we sketched three viable ingress patterns for Redwood Private in your VPCs and on your on-prem network:

1) AWS PrivateLink (NLB + mTLS) to expose a service endpoint in your VPC and enforce private connectivity.
2) VPC Peering between Redwood-managed VPC and Orion VPCs for direct, low-hop traffic.
3) Site-to-site VPN (IPSec) from Orion on-prem to our private gateway as a fallback/DR path.

Attached: a diagram (network-diagram.svg) and a short trade-offs doc (privatelink-peering-vpn-tradeoffs.pdf).

Request: can you confirm the following constraints so we can recommend a single path for the MVP pilot?
- Are Transit Gateway or Direct Connect links in use now?
- Any policy requiring explicit agent-level packet inspection in your DCs?
- Preferred MFA/mTLS setup or existing KMS for in-transit certs?

Plan: once we agree on constraints, Karthik will propose a recommended configuration (security controls, routing, failover behavior) and Marissa will scope the pilot timeline.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwood.com]

Attachments: network-diagram.svg (diagram), privatelink-peering-vpn-tradeoffs.pdf (3-page), pilot-plan-orion.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@orionhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Nguyen <bob.nguyen@orionhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reconciling multipath access for private inference: PrivateLink vs Peering vs S2S VPN

Jasmine —

Thanks for the summary. A few constraints from our side:
- We have an existing Direct Connect into our primary DCs but not into the AWS accounts used for dev/test. We do run a Transit Gateway for cross-account routing.
- Our security team requires that any inbound connections terminate on a dedicated (non-shared) NLB for auditability.
- On-prem packet inspection happens in a north-south appliance; we cannot mirror private keys to that device.
- DR requirement: we must have a non-cloud-native path (VPN over our MPLS) in event of cloud routing faults.

Questions:
1) If we do PrivateLink, can the endpoint be fronted by an NLB per your diagram and still meet mTLS termination requirements?
2) For VPC Peering, will we need to touch our routing tables in Transit Gateway, or can Redwood advertise prefixes to our TGW?

If you can answer those two, we can pick an approach for the pilot.

Best,
Alice
Alice Chen
Sr. Network Engineer — Orion Health Systems
alice.chen@orionhealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@orionhealth.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reconciling multipath access for private inference: PrivateLink vs Peering vs S2S VPN

Alice —

Short answers up front:
1) PrivateLink + NLB: Yes. We can provision a dedicated NLB in the Redwood account that sits behind the PrivateLink NVA and perform mTLS on the Redwood side. To satisfy your auditability ask, we recommend a per-customer NLB + per-customer endpoint service so logs are scoped. That preserves endpoint isolation and keeps your security appliance out of the private key path.

2) Peering + TGW: VPC Peering alone won't propagate routes to your Transit Gateway automatically. Two practical choices:
   a) Use TGW attachments on both sides and advertise Redwood prefixes into your TGW (requires a peering/TGW cross-account attachment and route updates).
   b) Use our side of a Transit VPC pattern where Redwood announces prefixes via a BGP session to your TGW — more operational work but scales for multi-account Orion footprint.

Trade-offs and my recommendation for the MVP pilot:
- Pilot recommendation: PrivateLink primary (lowest blast radius, minimal route churn) + site-to-site VPN for DR/failover.
  Rationale: meets your NLB/audit requirement, avoids touching TGW routing for the pilot, and gives a clear DR path you control.
- If ultra-low latency (sub-ms) across AZs is required later, we can evaluate TGW peering or Direct Connect options for a second phase.

Operational notes:
- We'll provide a runbook for endpoint provisioning, cert exchange (mTLS with mutual certs), and a heartbeat routing policy to prefer PrivateLink with automatic failover to VPN if the health checks on the PrivateLink NLB fail.
- Security: no private keys are shared with your packet inspection appliance; we support per-session mutual TLS using customer-managed certs (KMS/HSM integration optional).

Next steps I propose:
1) Alice confirms you can accept the PrivateLink + NLB model with per-customer endpoints.
2) Jasmine and I will draft the provisioning steps and a change window.
3) Marissa will propose pilot dates once we have confirmation.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@orionhealth.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reconciling multipath access for private inference: PrivateLink vs Peering vs S2S VPN

Alice —

Thanks for the clear constraints. We're aligned with Karthik's recommendation: PrivateLink (dedicated NLB + per-customer endpoint service) as the pilot, with an IPSec S2S VPN over your MPLS as the DR/failover path.

Operational asks from Redwood for the pilot:
- A short maintenance window (2 hours) in the week of July 12 for endpoint validation and certificate exchange.
- Access for a temporary BGP session if you want health-based route failover (optional).
- PO/contract signature to cover dedicated endpoint hours and data egress — Bob, can your procurement team confirm?

If Orion signs off on these three bullets, we'll lock the pilot scope and share the pilot-plan-orion.xlsx with timelines and success criteria.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Manager, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
